title: CLARA 2027 IFIP_SEC context-bound authorization receipt, version 1
description: Canonical typed commitment for one governed operation under the Replay-Closed Authorization study (paper: Replay-Closed Authorization Across Purpose, Delegation, and AI Proposal Lineage; blueprint arms B0-B4). The receipt binds tenant, authorizing principal, delegated actor, purpose, operation, AI proposal lineage hash, policy and consent epochs, a consume-once nonce, validity window and an HMAC signature profile. Purpose: the single structural contract for IFIP_SEC-X01 (Phase P02, RQ1); downstream tasks (X02 lineage digest, X03 nonce store, X04 context verify) consume these exact field names. Allowed input: one JSON object describing one receipt. Failure semantics: fail closed - any missing required field, unknown extra field, malformed hash/timestamp/identifier or unknown version rejects with a stable uppercase reason code from the shared stdlib validator (schema_validator.py). The stdlib 2020-12 subset has no cross-field comparison, so the temporal rule 'expiry strictly after issued_at' is encoded as strict UTC RFC 3339 timestamps here and ENFORCED by the composed validator in tests/test_receipt_schema.py (reason code TEMPORAL_ORDER); unparseable timestamps fail closed (TIMESTAMP_UNPARSEABLE). Replay protection (atomically consuming the nonce) and signature verification are downstream runtime duties, not schema duties. Versioning: additive-only within v1; the version field is a const so unknown versions are rejected. Security gate: the schema carries no credential material and no health value (no diagnosis, symptom, record or free-text clinical content); additionalProperties:false makes any such injected field a hard rejection.

version.description: Receipt contract version. Only '1' exists (additive-only evolution within v1); unknown versions fail closed with CONST_MISMATCH.

tenant.description: Tenant identifier scoping the receipt; cross-tenant replay is out of scope by construction. No whitespace or control characters.

principal.description: Authorizing principal (the consent/policy subject) whose epochs and purpose bound this receipt. Opaque identifier or e-mail-shaped label; never a credential.

purpose.description: Purpose-of-use label (snake_case, e.g. 'medication_management'). Purpose binding is part of the signed commitment; cross-purpose replay must be rejected downstream.

delegated_actor.description: Actor actually performing the operation under this receipt. For non-delegated use this equals 'principal'; multi-hop delegation chains are verified via the proposal lineage hash and ancestry checks (X02/X04), never by this field alone.

operation.description: Governed operation label in dotted lowercase form (e.g. 'medication.ddi_check'). The canonical operation registry is downstream; the schema fixes only the syntax.

proposal_lineage_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest binding this receipt to the AI proposal lineage (dispatch digest over the proposal chain incl. parent reference; computed by task X02). Lowercase 64-hex only.

policy_epoch.description: Policy epoch identifier in force at issuance (versioned GovernancePolicyEpoch label). Epoch interleavings are the RQ1 study variable.

consent_epoch.description: Versioned medical consent epoch identifier in force at issuance for (tenant, principal, purpose).

nonce.description: Consume-once replay nonce (URL-safe token, >=16 chars). Schema fixes syntax only; atomic single consumption is the X03 nonce store's linearizable duty.

issued_at.description: Issuance instant, strict UTC RFC 3339 ('Z' suffix, <=6 fractional digits) so the expiry ordering check is deterministic.

expiry.description: Expiry instant; MUST be strictly after issued_at. Enforced by the composed validator (TEMPORAL_ORDER) because the stdlib subset cannot compare two fields.

algorithm.description: Signature algorithm over the canonical serialization of every other field (blueprint: HMAC over actor, patient, tenant, purpose, task, consent/policy epoch, dispatch digest, nonce and parent reference).

value.description: HMAC-SHA256 output as lowercase 64-hex. Signature EQUALITY is checked downstream; this schema guarantees only well-formedness (fail closed on tamper-shaped values).
